It uses `containerChildren.get(i)` where `i` ranges from 0 to `childrenSize - 1`, and `childrenSize` is set to `containerChildren.size()`. The API documentation of `get` states it throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the index is out of range (index < 0 || index >= size()). Since the loop condition ensures `i` is always less than the current size, and `i` starts at 0 and never becomes negative, the index is always valid. Thus, the throwing condition is fully avoided by the loop bounds.
remark: The IndexOutOfBoundsException is avoided because the loop iterates using an index that strictly stays within the valid range [0, size()-1] based on the current size of the list at the start of the loop. No other exceptions are declared for the `get` method.
